newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber extends gains on Tokyo's rise.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber extends gains on Tokyo's rise.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed with extended gains following a firmer Tokyo futures market, dealers said.
They said the rainy season in Thailand which may cause further supply disruptions also helped keep sentiment firm.
"The market is moving up not because of buying interest but because of external factors," said one dealer.
She said concerns over the supply situation in Thailand, a leading producer, also kept sellers on the sidelines.
Dealers said trading was likely to remain quiet while market players await fresh incentives.

At the close, benchmark September RSS1 buyer was quoted at 326.50 cents ($1.31) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, up 2.50 cents from Monday. September SMR20 buyer was up 1.50 cents at 308.50 cents ($1.24) a kg.
Rates offered by trading houses were maintained throughout the day. The SMR20 was offered at 307 cents, SMR10 at 306, SMR5 at 316, SMR CV at 376, SMR L at 356 and drum latex FOB at 245-248.2
The INRO five-day average rose to 245.30 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Aug 26 from 245.16 on Aug 23. The daily indicator rose to 245.92 from 245.45. ($1=2.4930 ringgit)
